The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Historical September maxima in the region average near 32–34 °C, yet the current active monsoon phase supports the market-implied range. Final readings from official stations will resolve the market once the 24-hour period closes.

Official and ensemble forecasts from sources including the Japan Meteorological Agency, GFS, and private models consistently indicate a day of widespread precipitation and overcast skies driven by southerly flow and high humidity. This setup limits solar heating, with daytime highs projected near 26–27°C (roughly 78–81°F) amid 70–100% rain chances and dew points in the low-to-mid 20s°C. 

Model consensus shows limited daytime warming potential due to evaporative cooling and reduced insolation, though minor variations in rainfall timing or brief cloud breaks could nudge the peak slightly higher (toward 28°C) or lower (toward 25°C). Historical September norms for Tokyo feature highs near 28–29°C under clearer conditions, making the current wet pattern a clear downward driver relative to climatology. 

With resolution imminent and no major forecast shifts in the last 24 hours, trader sentiment reflects tight clustering around the 26–27°C outcomes as the most probable range given the stable, rain-dominated regime.

title: Highest temperature in Hong Kong on September 7?

Ensemble forecasts and recent model runs converge on a peak near 33°C, consistent with the 78.5% market-implied probability, while limited cloud cover and southeasterly flow reduce cooling potential compared to typical September climatology of 31.6°C. Updated observations from Changi station and surrounding sites show sustained warmth into early September, supporting trader consensus around the 33°C threshold over lower or higher outliers.

Clear to partly cloudy skies and low humidity support moderate maxima near seasonal norms, with no incoming fronts or heat advection expected to push readings higher. This alignment explains the 72.5% market-implied probability for 25°C and secondary weighting on 26°C, as traders weigh slight model spread in peak afternoon temperatures against historical early-September baselines. Updated runs through September 6 reinforce this range ahead of final observations.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lemd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from AEMET and ensemble models place Madrid’s September 8 maximum near 34–35 °C under clear skies, light southwesterly flow, and strong daytime heating beneath a persistent subtropical ridge. This setup favors rapid surface warming after a cool start near 21 °C, with peak readings expected in the afternoon when solar insolation and urban heat-island effects are strongest. Minor model spread arises from slight differences in boundary-layer mixing and exact wind timing, keeping the 35 °C and 36 °C outcomes nearly tied in trader pricing. Historical early-September averages near 28–29 °C underscore the anomalous warmth, while the next 24–48 hours of high-resolution runs will refine whether any last-minute adjustment pushes the daily high across the 35.5 °C threshold used for market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=wmkk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from Malaysia's Meteorological Department and numerical models converge on a daytime high near 33°C for Kuala Lumpur on September 8, consistent with the market's leading 47% implied probability for that outcome and 35% for 34°C. Typical early-September climatology features mean highs of 31–32°C under the influence of the southwest monsoon, with peak readings occasionally reaching 34–35°C when skies clear and insolation is strong. Scattered thunderstorms and haze expected on the 8th should limit extreme heating by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling, though brief afternoon breaks could still allow brief spikes. Low probabilities assigned to 35°C or higher reflect the narrow historical window above 34°C and the moderating effects of regional moisture. Updated model runs and official briefings in the next 24–48 hours will refine these trader-implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and ensemble model guidance indicate clearing skies and moderate onshore flow will support a high temperature in the mid-to-upper 80s across Los Angeles on September 8, following scattered rain and cooler conditions on the 6th. Typical September marine-layer influence and west-southwest winds of 15-25 mph should cap inland peaks near 90°F while keeping coastal and downtown readings several degrees lower, consistent with climatological averages around 76°F but elevated by post-frontal warming. Traders have priced the 86-87°F bin highest because short-range runs cluster there, though marine-layer depth and exact wind timing introduce enough variability to sustain secondary probability on adjacent 84-85°F and 88-89°F outcomes. Updated model cycles and afternoon observations through the 7th remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on the highest temperature in Panama City on September 8 centers on 33°C and 34°C, with implied probabilities of 32.5% and 33.0% respectively, amid uncertainty in short-range forecasts. Recent model runs highlight variability in afternoon cloud cover and convective rainfall typical of Panama's rainy season, which can suppress peak temperatures below the 30–32°C climatological average or allow brief clearing for readings near 34°C. Steadier easterly flow and limited moisture convergence in some guidance support the slight edge for 34°C, while persistent showers in others favor 33°C. Updated regional model outputs and satellite observations over the next 48 hours will likely refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.
